The main takeaway from our work is that
the CNO abundances in low- and intermediate mass stars are determined primarily by deep circulation mixing during the RGB and the AGB stages.

deep circulation mixing is required to reproduce the observed trends of the CNO abundances with stellar mass on the RGB and ABB, and that the observed abundances are consistent with a single mechanism for deep circulation mixing, i.e., with the same mixing efficiency and same mixing depth for all low- and intermediate mass stars.
the observed abundances of the CNO elements are best reproduced by the assumption that the convective mixing in red giants is more extensive than that predicted by standard stellar evolution theory.
